amend.append: AMENDED (W47-FB-DOUBLE-STOP-OBSERVATION, native observation only; not a proof, no Quirin verdict moves, not an upstream defect claim): a harness driving only the public flb_* API (docs/reports/w47-fb-double-stop-observation/), linked against a Clang 21 -O0 debug libfluent-bit.so built from the 90978ac6 export and from the 046accf6 prepared clone (flb_lib.c, flb_engine.c, flb_fips.c, flb_input.c, flb_config.c and mk_utils.c byte-identical), with an LD_PRELOAD interposer logging every pthread_create/pthread_join and a gdb cross-check, 20 runs per scenario per tree under a 60 s watchdog (0 fired): (i) OBSERVED under an injected engine start failure (a dummy input given a property its config map does not declare, so flb_input_init_all fails on the engine thread): flb_start returned -1 after do_start joined the engine thread at src/flb_lib.c:999, and flb_stop joined the same identifier again at :1058 (no create between the two), 40/40 debug runs; glibc 2.43 returned 0 for the second join and the process exited 0; a ThreadSanitizer build aborted at that join (CHECK failed in ThreadRegistry::ConsumeThreadUserId, exit 66) 20/20. (iii) OBSERVED for the flb_fips_init arm (security.fips_mode=on on a host with no OpenSSL FIPS provider): flb_start returned -1 before the spawn, ctx->config->worker read 0, and flb_stop's join at :1058 of identifier 0 ended in SIGSEGV inside pthread_join (exit 139) 40/40; TSan CHECK failed at the same join 20/20; the mk_utils_worker_spawn-failure arm is not reachable from the public API without fault injection and was not exercised. (v) OBSERVED: start (0), stop, stop joined the engine thread at :1077 and again at :1058, 40/40 (glibc returned 0 both times, exit 0); TSan CHECK failed at the second 20/20. Control (start 0, one stop) joined the engine thread exactly once (:1077), 40/40 debug, and ran clean under TSan 20/20. (ii) and (iv) were not exercised (the TSan control does not run flb_stop against a concurrently exiting engine). The entry stays open for (ii) and (iv); (i), (iii) and (v) are now natively observed and remain candidates, not defect claims.
